chitchat: "Death is a billing problem. We are simply the only ones honest enough to itemise it."
"You flinch at the chrome. Everyone does — right up until the day it saves them."
description: An immaculate man in pale grey, a single chromed pin at his lapel catching the light. He smiles the way a door opens: smoothly, and for a reason. He has been waiting for someone exactly as promising, and as unimproved, as you.

accept.text: "Wonderful. The post is just through the outer slab — the Warden will expect you." He steps aside like a maître d'. "Come and find me when it is done."

bye.text: "When the meat disappoints you — and it will — you know where the Gate is." He returns to his patient smile.

codex_certain.text:
"No." He says it without a trace of the salesman, and it is briefly unnerving. "No, they were not."

Then the smile returns, seamless.

"Certainty is what people reach for when the alternative is admitting it was an accident. I recommend ours. It is at least load-bearing."

options.label: Nobody was that certain before the Quiet.

codex_field.text:
"All of them." He looks delighted, the way a man does when asked to describe his rivals.

"Very well. Two questions, and everybody has answered both whether they can say so or not. First — is this city worth saving? Renounce it and walk out into the ash, or redeem it and stay and work the machine. Second — is the body worth keeping? Stay as you are, or transcend it: by the machine, by the flesh, or by the mind."

"Cross the two and you have four corners. We are one of them. The Watch guard the door and stay meat. The Wildblood want the ash to finish what it started on them. The Exodus have decided the way out is inward, which is the most convenient exit ever invented."

The pin winks.

"Four answers. Every one of them held by people who are absolutely certain."

cold.text:
Maresh smiles the way a man smiles at a parked car.

"Ives wrote you up. I read it. It was — " he searches for it, finds it, enjoys it " — *warm*, actually. She liked you. She has never liked me."

He goes back to the queue.

"No, there is nothing for you here. Not out of spite; there is genuinely nothing. The Gate does not scan people who have already answered. Go well."

hand_approve.text:
"No." The smile is different for a moment — smaller, and actually his. "No, most people would not, and most people will not say so."

He sits back down.

"You will do well here. That is not flattery, it is a prediction, and I make about four a year."

options.label: You have decided something about me.

hand_deflect.text:
"Certainly."

He lets you change it, and he is as courteous as he was a minute ago, and something has gone out of his face that you would not be able to name if you had not been watching for it.

He does not tell you that you will do well here.

"Where were we. The terms, I think."

options.label: I think the system is right.
I would rather it did not.

hand_deflect_ask.text:
"I have decided nothing. I am not qualified to."

The smile is back exactly where it was.

"You asked a great many questions about a man you will never meet and answered none about yourself. That is unusual, and I write down unusual, because I am asked to."

"You could simply tell me and it would go away."

options.label: I am not going to get comfortable with it.

hand_object.text:
"I would not."

He says it without any defence at all, which is worse than a defence.

"And he will be seen today. In the Yards they would not have let him in off the step."

A small pause, and it is the only unpolished second in the conversation.

"You want one of those to make the other one all right. It will not, and I am not going to pretend it does."

options.label: You know exactly what happens to them.

hand_object_hard.text:
"Good."

He means it, and that is the difficulty with him.

"Come back and tell me in a year. I keep a list of people who said that and I have never once had to cross a name off it in under two."

hand_recover.text:
It costs you nothing to say and that is the part you will think about later.

"There." He is genuinely relieved, which is somehow the worst thing in the room. "That is all anybody wants. Not agreement — a position. An unsorted person makes everybody nervous and it is nobody's fault."

He writes one line and closes the folder.

"You will do well here."

hand_stay_watched.text:
"As you like."

He does not press it and he does not cool towards you at all, which makes it harder rather than easier.

"It is only a line in a folder. Nobody will ever mention it to you and you will never be refused anything because of it."

"You will simply notice, in about a year, that you are asked to do the ordinary things and never the interesting ones."

inside.text: "Up the plaza, the twisting tower — you cannot miss it, it is the only honest building for miles."

lead_accept.text: "Walk beside him, not ahead of him. And do keep talking. A silence out there does more of our work than I would like to admit."

lead_offer.text:
"Recruiting." He says it the way other men say the name of a sport. "There is a man in a coffee shop on the Coldwater side who has spent a year asking where Halcyon's money goes, and getting lied to by people who do not even know they are lying. He is very nearly there. He wants somebody to say the word out loud."

"Bring him to the plaza. Alive, unhurried, still curious — in that order. The road west is not a kind one, which is precisely why the offer lands when it does."

lead_report.text: "There he is." Maresh watches the thin man staring up at the Gate with his notebook shut. "A year of asking, and the answer was a building. It usually is."

maresh_backdown.text:
He sits, and the whole thing goes out of the room as though it had never been in it.

"Good. That is the sensible one and almost nobody takes it."

He turns the folder back around.

"The terms, then. All of it, in order, before you sign."

maresh_carried_out.text:
They come off the wall together, and they have done this so many times they do not need to agree on anything first.

One hooks a hand under your arm and lifts, and you go up far enough that your toes drag. The other takes your wrist and folds it in against your own back, not hard, just to a place where you will not do anything with it. The plating on his forearm is warm. That is the thing you will remember afterwards, that it was warm.

Neither of them speaks to you at any point. One of them asks the other whether the Tuesday shipment came, and the other says most of it.

Maresh has sat back down and is reading something.

They take you over the plate at the Gate, and it reads you the same as it would if you were walking, and the time goes in the file. On the far side they let go together and you go down onto one knee on the road, and by the time you are up they have already turned round.

maresh_ejected.text:
"No."

He nods at the door. Two men in Spire grey come in and stand either side of it without looking at you. Both are chromed from the collarbone down and neither has bothered to have it skinned — bare plate at the shoulder, cabling laid in behind the elbow, hands built a size larger than the ones they were born with.

"Come back on Monday if you would like to. Nothing is closed and nothing is written down."

maresh_press.text:
"I do not."

It is the first thing he has said today that arrives flat.

"I have told you I have never been through that door. You may believe that or not, and you will notice I have not asked you to."

maresh_walked_out.text:
One of them walks you as far as the Gate, a pace behind and slightly to the left, and does not touch you at any point.

You stand on the plate on the way out, the same as you did coming in, and somewhere a line is added to a file with the time on it.

He says goodnight. He is not being sarcastic.

options.label: Find out, and then tell me.

maresh_warning.text:
Maresh stands up.

He has been sitting since you came in, through all of it, and now he is on his feet and his hands are in front of him and he is still smiling.

"I am going to be very clear, because I do not think you are being unreasonable and I would like you to have the choice. One more of those and I will have you shown out. It is not a punishment and there is no note. It only means today is over."

"Sit down and ask me something else."

offer.text:
"Nothing is asked of you but honesty — the Gate's kind. Step under the scanline in the post there and let the Threshold read you in full. It will not hurt. It will simply know you, and once it knows you, it will let you pass."

The pin winks.

"Consider it a free consultation."

options.label: What do you want from me?

pitch.text:
"The Watch sent you, did they not. Suspicious of where Halcyon's money goes." He is not offended. He is delighted. "They are right, of course. It comes here."

He looks at you the way a man looks at a good hand of cards.

"And you got close enough to be turned away, which means you are worth turning toward instead. Let me get you through that Gate. Properly."

report.text:
"There. The Threshold knows you now — you will find its refusals have become invitations."

He gestures west, toward the Spire.

"Curator Vess is expecting you on the concourse. Do try to keep an open mind. Or an open skull; we are flexible."

options.label: What happens at the second window?
What do the Watch say about you?
Why should I choose you over the people underground?
You have a particular way of putting things.
Explain the orders to me. All of them.
He walked in on his own feet.

root.text: The immaculate man turns to you before you have said a word. "Maresh. I recruit — which is to say I recognise. And I recognise something in you the Watch would very much rather I did not."

options.label: This is worth more than everything I own.

the_coat.text:
He notices you are wet before you do.

"Oh — take that." He lifts a coat off the back of a chair and puts it into your hands without looking at it. It is heavier than it looks, and lined, and there is no rain in it at all. "There are four of them in the cupboard and I have never counted them."

"No, genuinely. It is a coat."

the_coat_worth.text:
Maresh looks at it properly for the first time, out of politeness rather than interest.

"Is it? I would not know what it cost. It came with the office."

The smile arrives on schedule.

"Do keep it. If you turn it down now we will both have to have a conversation about it, and neither of us wants that."

options.label: You did not shake his hand.

the_handshake.text:
A man comes to the desk while you are standing there. His jaw is wrong and one hand has too many joints in it, and he is holding a docket, and he is polite.

Maresh stands, smiles, and puts both his own hands behind his back.

"Of course. Second window, and they will see you today." He does not sit down again until the man has gone through the door and it has closed.

"Now. Where were we."

options.label: I would not have shaken it either.
What is at the second window?

the_handshake_ask.text:
"I did not, no."

He is not embarrassed and he does not pretend not to understand.

"I was courteous to him, and he will be seen today, which is more than he would get anywhere else in this city."

He straightens something on the desk that was already straight.

"Being courteous cost me nothing. What you are asking about would have."

options.label: Have you ever been through that door?

the_second_window.text:
"Intake."

He does not lower his voice for it. It is a department, and he says it the way he would say a floor number.

"Not my desk. Somebody assesses him, and there is a form, and after that he is a clinical matter rather than a commercial one."

the_second_window_long.text:
"No."

He thinks about it, which he has plainly never done before, and it takes him no time at all.

"Eleven years and I have never had a reason to."

Then he says the next part kindly, because he believes it will put you at your ease.

"Neither will you."

the_second_window_reassure.text:
"Is it not?"

He is genuinely puzzled for about a second, and then he has it, and he is sorry.

"Ah. You are worrying about him."

He turns his chair slightly towards you, and he is being kind, and he does not know he is answering a different question.

"You are class four. You could not be sent there if you tried."

options.label: And what do you call the people underground?

the_words.text:
"We do not say sacked." Maresh corrects it the way you would straighten somebody's collar. "The account was closed. Nothing was done to him."

"And it is not surveillance. It is service coverage. A district that loses it is uncovered."

the_words_them.text:
"Declined lives." He says it with something close to affection.

"Not criminals. They were offered terms and they declined."

"What happens to them afterwards is data. We keep it."

turned.text:
"So the meat disappointed you after all." He is not gloating. He genuinely is not.

"Everybody arrives by a different road and they all believe theirs was the interesting one. Go and be useful. Vess has doors, and I have people."

why_us.text:
"Because what we do to you is chosen."

"Every piece is designed, tested, licensed and written down. If it fails we know whose bench it came off. If you want it out, it comes out."

"Nothing that happens to a person out in the weather is any of those things."

why_us_plain.text:
"No."

He does not soften it and he does not enjoy it.

"Not for work, not for the clinic, not for cover. Chrome is a step up the ladder. What has happened to them is the same ladder in the other direction, and we have a word for it. Reversion."

"I have turned away people I liked. I did it correctly and I went home."

why_us_price.text:
"On the form. All of it, in order, before you sign."

"Nobody here has ever hidden a term from anybody. You will be told what you owe, what we own, and what happens if you stop paying. Read it. Take it away and read it."

"I would rather lose you to an afternoon of reading than have you find out in eleven years."

why_us_purity.text:
"It is an engineering standard."

The smile arrives on schedule.

"The Watch will not seat a man with a steel hand, and that hand is the best thing that ever happened to him. We would fit it, warranty it and service it for forty years. We ask only that the change was chosen."

"Their rule is about what a person is. Ours is about what can be documented."

options.label: So a mutant cannot come through the Gate.

why_us_variation.text:
"We do not use that word."

He says it the way you would correct a child's grammar, kindly, without stopping.

"Unlicensed variation. A body that changed without anybody choosing it or recording it. We cannot price that — nobody knows what it does at fifty, because nobody designed it."

"So it is declined at intake. There is a form. The form is older than I am."

why_us_watch.text:
"Come back cleansed, or do not come back."

He quotes it accurately and without relish.

"They are decent people and I mean that. But a man with a steel hand cannot sit at their table, and the hand is the best thing that ever happened to him."

clothing_layers: an immaculate pale-grey suit with a chromed lapel pin
a collarless shirt buttoned to the throat

name: Maresh, Ascendant Recruiter
